a private registry key for an OPSYN snapshot (508b26d5a): byte 1, which no SNOBOL4 name holds, then the name, so the alias resolver's rt_proc_find reaches the snapshot while rt_proc_is_registered(NEW) stays false; one name compared whole, never split, and the one test of its first byte only recognises such a key -- not an aggregate (ruled by the cfo, census owner, 2026-10-02 on CEO-1444; a typed cure is FNCBLK holding the snapshot's index)

UNLOAD's tombstone convention (\x01<unloaded> above) for the registry slot module_init keeps for a skipped procedure (38a4375a3): a name no lookup finds; the procedure name after the marker is for a reader of the binary and is never split back out -- not an aggregate (ruled by the cfo, census owner, 2026-10-02 on CEO-1444; a typed cure is an inert-slot flag on the registry record, for the tombstone too)

ONE name that holds a NUL byte, or begins with byte 1, spelled as a C-string key: byte 1, then the hex of its bytes (eb92ef197, CEO-1412), so $, the namespace and every capture reach one cell; an injective spelling of a single value, compared whole, never decoded or split, and NV_name_needs_key's first-byte test is the escape that keeps it injective -- not an aggregate (ruled by the cfo, census owner, 2026-10-02 on CEO-1444; a typed cure is a variable table keyed by the counted name)
